summary: Replace the random local search with a structured construction: simplex-shaped digit-vector sets {x in Z_{>=0}^k : sum x_i <= n}, embedded in integers with base 2n+1. The program evaluates every (k, n) with at most 4000 points and returns the best one.

Raise the size cap from 3000 to 4000 points. Centre each embedded set (subtract half its max value) so the 1e15 magnitude limit allows roughly twice the range, and filter candidates by their actual maximum value instead of the loose (2n+1)^k bound. These changes admit larger and higher-dimensional s

I added a second family of candidates, truncated simplices {x ≥ 0 : sum x ≤ n, each x_i ≤ m}, embedded with the smaller base 2m+1. Their sizes are counted by DP, so only sets of 1500–4000 points are built and scored. This lets higher-dimensional shapes fit within the 4000-point cap. I also restrict

After the simplex search picks the best set, I add a time-bounded local search that removes points whose removal raises log|A-A|/log|A+A|. Each pass estimates every point's loss in sums and differences from representation counts, removes a batch of the most promising points, and keeps the batch only

Besides plain simplices, I now also try weighted simplices {x ≥ 0 : Σ w_i x_i ≤ n} with weights 1, 2 and 3. Each coordinate gets a mixed-radix base sized to its own range, and only sets of 2000–4000 points are scored. The plain-simplex candidates are scored first, so the previous best is still reach

After the simplex search, I take the best (k, n) and try embeddings with smaller bases B between n+1 and 2n. Collisions in the embedding can merge sums more than differences, which may raise the ratio. Any improvement is kept, and the first pass now stops at 50 seconds to leave time for this.

I now keep the top three (k, n) simplex candidates from the first pass and run the smaller-base tuning on each, splitting the time budget between them instead of tuning only the best. The embedding is vectorised with numpy to make this faster.

I added a family of "shell" sets, {x ≥ 0 : n−w ≤ Σx ≤ n} with 0 < w < n, which sit between a plain simplex and a lower-dimensional simplex slice. They are scored after the simplex pass and before base tuning, within time limits. Plain simplices and slices are unchanged.
